clue.text: When making comeback, some overuse botox? Certainly

indicators.note: making a comeback means going back the way you came, so the letters are read right to left
only some of the following words are wanted, a run of letters tucked inside them

blocks.note: a run of letters straddling the two words, read forwards

explanation.surface: A cosmetic patient keeps coming back for more injections, and someone wonders whether they are overdoing the botox.
explanation.walkthrough: Read overUSE BOTox backwards and TO BE SURE appears.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic way of agreeing, a stock Irish-flavoured idiom meaning without doubt.

clue.text: Plath poem recited, Chomp with Part of Mouth

indicators.note: recited means spoken out, so what follows is judged by ear

blocks.note: the lips form part of the mouth

explanation.surface: Reading a Sylvia Plath poem aloud while chewing.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEW LIPS said quickly gives the flower name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulips is a 1961 poem by Sylvia Plath, written in hospital about flowers she was given.

clue.text: Reportedly purchase permit to get around city

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the next word counts by its sound

explanation.surface: Reports that you need to buy a permit to drive around a town.
explanation.definitionFit: A road that bypasses a town avoids going through it, circling around instead.

clue.text: For starters, Scrubs, Oz, American Dad! are revolutionary kind of TV

indicators.note: starters are first letters, of the next two words here
a revolution turns things around, so the word before is turned back to front

blocks.note: pop is a word for father
taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: A claim that three American TV series broke new ground in television.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrubs, Oz and American Dad! are real shows, which makes them look like the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running serial drama genre on television, originally sponsored by soap makers.

clue.text: Derby cameramen drunk at solemn occasion

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: TV crew from Derby turning up inebriated at a sombre ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby is an English city, here just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Remembrance Day, 11 November, is a grave commemoration of the war dead with silence and wreaths.

clue.text: At first, servant can help out and pull something, heavily

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each of the next two words
out suggests something put out of order, so the word before it is rearranged

explanation.surface: A domestic servant pitches in to help haul something heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: SCHLEP is a Yiddish borrowing common in American and British English.
explanation.definitionFit: To schlep is to drag or carry a load laboriously, a colloquial verb of effortful hauling.

clue.text: Prickly sorts, front of cast at start of play

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: Act I is how a play begins

explanation.surface: Bad-tempered actors line up at the curtain-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Prickly sorts sounds like touchy people; it means spiny plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Cacti are spiny desert plants, literally prickly specimens, with a nod to irritable people.

clue.text: Survive … hold on … no hint of recovery … then this?

definitions.text: Survive … hold on … no hint of recovery … then this?

indicators.note: no means without, so a letter is taken out
a hint is just a trace, the opening letter

blocks.note: to grasp something is to keep a firm grip on it

explanation.surface: A patient fighting to survive, clinging on with no sign of getting better.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a dying moment as well as building the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A last gasp is the final breath before death, the end of a struggle to stay alive.

clue.text: Instances of fabrication producing hats

blocks.note: first meaning: lies, in Cockney rhyming slang
second meaning: flat-topped hats with a round brim

explanation.surface: Fabricating something that turns out to be headwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Fabrication looks like manufacturing; it means lying. Pork pies rhymes with lies in British rhyming slang.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, porkies are untruths, while a pork-pie hat is a style with a low crown, named for the pastry.

clue.text: Dimmer sun might rise ... after this?

definitions.text: Dimmer sun might rise ... after this?

indicators.note: to rise is to rebel, throwing the letters into disorder

explanation.surface: A wistful thought that the sun comes up weaker once the year turns past its longest day.
explanation.walkthrough: After the summer solstice the days shorten, so the whole clue describes the answer as well as spelling it.
explanation.definitionFit: Midsummer night is the shortest night of the year, after which daylight wanes and the sun weakens.

clue.text: Salve composed of lithium, lead, aluminium and teensiest bit of magnesium

indicators.note: the tiniest bit of a word is just its opening letter

blocks.note: chemical symbol for lead, from Latin plumbum

explanation.surface: A worrying list of ingredients for an ointment: toxic metals plus a pinch of magnesium.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a chemistry label; each metal is reduced to its symbol from the periodic table.
explanation.definitionFit: A balm for chapped lips is a soothing ointment, which is exactly what a salve is.

clue.text: In Channel Isles, traces of some old ruined cutter

indicators.note: a trace is the faintest mark left behind, so just the opening letter of each following word

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: Archaeologists in Jersey or Guernsey find remnants of an old wrecked boat.
explanation.walkthrough: A cutter sounds like a small sailing vessel in a ruined state; it is really a tooth. The Channel Islands are British islands off Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: An incisor is a front tooth with a sharp edge used for biting through food, hence a cutter.

clue.text: Extremely palatable sauce that’s often seen in starters?

definitions.text: Extremely palatable sauce that’s often seen in starters?

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, the first and last letters of the next word
starters are the opening letters of the words just before

explanation.surface: A tasty sauce that turns up on many restaurant first courses.
explanation.walkthrough: Starters looks like the menu course, but it asks for the first letters of sauce, that's and often.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is a basil and pine-nut sauce, very tasty and a regular feature of Italian appetisers and pasta dishes.

clue.text: Pop star into opium losing head, addled, becoming less clear

indicators.note: into says the first item goes inside the second
losing its head means the first letter is dropped
addled means muddled, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, then trimmed and jumbled
Sting, singer formerly of the Police

explanation.surface: A rock singer on drugs, befuddled and getting hazier.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass or a view misting up is clouding over with condensation, so growing less transparent.

clue.text: The seminar is about an artist

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: A lecture series devoted to a particular painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was the French painter and sculptor, a leading figure of Fauvism.

clue.text: A small island’s in these empty Australian waters!

indicators.note: empty means hollowed out, keeping only the outside letters
in puts the first part inside the second

blocks.note: the possessive ending, taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a tiny island sitting in a deserted stretch of southern ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tasman Sea is the stretch of ocean between Australia and New Zealand.

clue.text: Top Tory supports Article delivering seat of power to Europeans

indicators.note: in a down entry, what supports sits underneath, so it comes second

blocks.note: William Hague, once leader of the Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A senior Conservative backs an item of legislation that hands power to Brussels.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is a British Conservative; William Hague led the party from 1997 to 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hague hosts the Dutch government and international courts, a centre of authority in the Netherlands.

clue.text: Either of two writers to be annoying online, unblocked for the most part

indicators.note: only most of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to troll is to provoke people on the internet

explanation.surface: Two authors misbehaving on social media once their accounts are unblocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope wrote Victorian novels and Joanna Trollope writes modern ones, so the surname fits both.

clue.text: Old author ashen? Mr Sheen will refresh

indicators.note: refreshing something gives it a new form, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: all twelve letters, rearranged; Mr Sheen is a British furniture polish brand

explanation.surface: An elderly writer looks grey, but a squirt of household polish will perk him up.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Sheen is a UK spray polish, so the surface is a cleaning advert.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermann Hesse was the German novelist of Siddhartha and Steppenwolf, who died in 1962.

clue.text: Where prince said he could be seen running (with no hint of running)

definitions.text: Where prince said he could be seen

indicators.note: with no means without, so a letter comes out
a hint is just a trace, the opening letter

blocks.note: a machine that is running is working

explanation.surface: A royal alibi about where he was, wrapped in a nod to his jogging.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Andrew claimed he was at a Pizza Express in Woking, a commuter town in Surrey, on a disputed night.
explanation.definitionFit: In a 2019 interview the prince named this Surrey town as his location, at a pizza restaurant.

clue.text: Either of two pilots River Island’s taken on

indicators.note: taking something on means taking it in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast

explanation.surface: River Island, a British clothing chain, has hired a couple of pilots.
explanation.walkthrough: River Island is a UK fashion retailer, which hides the two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Orville and Wilbur Wright flew the first powered aeroplane, so the surname fits both aviators.

clue.text: Passage ceded regularly in own sweet time

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter, at fixed intervals
in places the chosen letters inside the following word

blocks.note: a hall is a corridor or passageway

explanation.surface: Someone gives way in a corridor, taking their own sweet time about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In own sweet time' reads as an idiom for dawdling; the definition is the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Halloween is the autumn festival of trick-or-treating, when children collect candy, so a season of sweets.

clue.text: Nothing good published about The Observer perhaps

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the one before

blocks.note: a paper that ran a story published it

explanation.surface: A grumble that nothing decent has been printed about the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a newspaper or periodical that voices views, so a Sunday paper is one example.

clue.text: Affair, maybe – often unethical romance, primarily?

definitions.text: Affair, maybe – often unethical romance, primarily?

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so the opening letter of each preceding word

explanation.surface: A musing that a love affair is usually an immoral romance.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An amour is a secret love affair, typically an illicit one, borrowed from French.

clue.text: American state that’s next to Russia

blocks.note: first meaning: the southern US state with Atlanta as capital
second meaning: the Caucasus country bordering Russia to the south

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one place, but the US state and the former Soviet republic share the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a southeastern US state and to a Caucasus republic sharing a border with Russia.

clue.text: Actor who’s started to honk a bit?

definitions.text: who’s started to honk a bit?

blocks.note: first meaning: Ryan, star of La La Land and Barbie

blocks.clueFragment: who’s started to honk a bit?
blocks.note: second meaning: a young goose, just beginning to find its voice

explanation.surface: An actor whose voice is beginning to crack.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a cryptic second meaning: a baby bird that will grow into a honker.
explanation.definitionFit: Ryan is a Canadian film star with this surname, and the word also names a young goose, a bird that honks.

clue.text: Watching the old getting home, for example, to give accommodation

indicators.note: giving accommodation means housing a guest, so one item holds the others

explanation.surface: Observing an elderly person being found a place to live.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeing is looking at something closely or with interest, a verb of observing.

clue.text: Sound, sounded sound

indicators.note: sounded means said out, so the next word is heard rather than read

blocks.note: a sound is a narrow sea channel, a strait

explanation.walkthrough: The same word three times in three senses: honest, spoken, and a stretch of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight and sound both describe someone honest and reliable, and a straight argument is a solid one.
